newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China to send large contingent of troops to HK.
newsitem.headline: China to send large contingent of troops to HK.

text.p: Communist China will send 4,000 troops streaming into Hong Kong by land, sea and air just hours after the wealthy British colony is handed over to Beijing at midnight on June 30.

The troops, backed by helicopters, ships and armoured personnel carriers, will cross the northern border at three points on July 1, Hong Kong's first day of Chinese rule since Britain seized the island colony in 1841.

It was a far larger number than previous estimates for the troops which would arrive on the first day. The announcement was made by the office of Tung Chee-hwa, China's handpicked Chief Executive-designate for the territory.
Outgoing British Governor Chris Patten quickly denounced the decision to send in such a large body of troops, backed by such an impressive arsenal.
"It doesn't sound to me the right sort of signal to send to the international community and above all I think it is a most appalling signal to send to the people of Hong Kong," he told reporters.

The forces of the People's Liberation Army (PLA) will start crossing the border six hours after Prince Charles, heir to the British throne, formally gives up the fiercely capitalist colony of 6.4 million people to China.

The PLA troops will be stationed in former British barracks around the territory. Britain kept as many as 10,000 troops in its colony on China's southern coast but they have dwindled to fewer than 1,000 in recent months.
The announcement said the PLA forces would be backed by 10 ships, six helicopters, 21 armoured cars and 400 other vehicles.
The PLA has 196 advance troops in Hong Kong already and 509 more will join them just before the midnight handover ceremony on June 30.
Patten said he would try to stop China from making such as show of force but there is little he can do in the final days of British rule.
He said: "I do think that it is most unfortunate that this decision has been made. We will continue to make representation and hope that this decision is reversed.
"I think I'm right in saying the arrival of the armoured personnel carriers will more or less coincide with the evening network news in the United States of America."
Patten has said in the past that PLA troops were largely unnecessary in Hong Kong. He repeated that internal security was a job for the police and noted that Hong Kong was a peaceful community.
In Beijing, China's Ministry of Defence declined to comment on the statement from Tung's office.
